An experiment was performed to investigate whether capillary action could account for the movement of water from roots to leaves in a plant.
The diagram shows apparatus used to model this effect using narrow glass capillary tubing. The inner diameter of the capillary tubing is $0.5 \text{ mm}$.
The initial height of the water in the tubing was recorded as $0.2 \text{ cm}$. After $2 \text{ minutes}$ the height was recorded as $1.8 \text{ cm}$.
The model assumes the rate of movement is constant.
What is the rate of water movement in $\text{mm}^3 \text{ min}^{-1}$ and what vessel type transfers water from roots to leaves in a real plant?

|  | rate of water movement / $\text{mm}^3 \text{ min}^{-1}$ | vessel type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | $0.5\pi$ | xylem |
| B | $0.5\pi$ | phloem |
| C | $\pi$ | xylem |
| D | $\pi$ | phloem |
| E | $2\pi$ | xylem |
| F | $2\pi$ | phloem |
| G | $4\pi$ | xylem |
| H | $4\pi$ | phloem |
